Round 412 passed C and the gate published it as `107eb2d`, so the next task (round 413) is written and the decision is **CONTINUE**. No app source was changed; the store tree is still clean.

**What I checked:**
- **C round 412:** PASS, 14 rows, real browser at 1440×900 and 1280×720, 0 bugs.
- **PERF-15b-i is done.** I closed A-R411-REVIEW-M1, L1, L3, L4 and TL-R412-L-F on that evidence.
- **Archive:** the round-412 task is saved as `tasks/round-412.md`, a byte-identical copy.
- **Regression:** not due until the first planning on or after 2026-11-10. RETRO is at round 416.

**Round 413 = PERF-15b-ii-a.** It is the last client stage of PERF-15, and PERF-15 closes when C passes it. A applies a reviewed patch byte for byte (`b-round-412/sketch-413.patch.txt`, sha `a7913dec…`, 9 files):
- **4 MiB cap while streaming:** the peaks file is read in chunks and dropped above 4 MiB, even when the server sends no size or a compressed size. An abort now also stops a body that has stalled.
- **Purchased stems:** a stem can carry a `peaksUrl`. It is only used when it is on the same host as the stem's audio; otherwise the waveform falls back to decoding. The purchased fetch also carries the peaks request, so its sign-in header is kept.
- **Tests:** PP7d is rewritten, because the old version faked `response.json()`, which the new code no longer calls; it is stricter now. New rows are PP7e, PP10–PP12b, PPC12, PK1–PK4 and PS18.
- **Docs:** docs 263 and 264 and the new doc 265 are marked Completed (C round 413 PASS).

**Checks on the patch before handing it to A:**
- typecheck and lint pass.
- The 24 related test files pass, 436/436, and the full suite passes, 3,922/3,922.
- All 15 deliberate breakages turn their expected test red.
- The demo waveform probes (normal, missing file, 8-bit file) give the same results as round 412 at both window sizes.
- The tech-lead reviewed it twice and found nothing Medium or higher; its two Lows are fixed.

**C will verify in round 413:**
- the 15 breakages turn the expected tests red on A's tree;
- the demo waveform probes still give the round-412 results at both window sizes;
- lane actions still work, and the paid Studio page still asks for sign-in;
- the three doc status lines are exact, and no screen file changes.

**Decisions and gaps:**
- **Firefox check:** Firefox isn't installed on the runner, so this check is now a manual item (TLM-PERF15-FIREFOX), and I asked root to install it. PERF-15 still closes on C's pass, because falling back to decoding is safe and already shown in Chrome. A Firefox crash would reopen it.
- **The size cap has no browser check.** Two attempts to serve a body with no reliable size failed: a redirect to a local server was never served, and Chrome did not decode a faked gzip body. The cap is covered by unit tests and the breakage runs only. I wrote no browser assert I couldn't run.
- **Same-host rule:** the backend must serve `peaksUrl` from the stem audio's host, or users lose the speed-up (playback still works). I wrote this into `docs/technical/studio-real-workspace/perf-15-backend-peaks-handoff.md`.

  - An architecture check at the end of PERF-15 (ARCH-CHECKPOINT-PERF15-PEAKS) asks whether the waveform-source logic should stay in the main Studio context.
  - Two Lows moved to the later polish list.
- **Process slip:** I committed to my scratch copy while the tech-lead was running its own breakage tests in it, which picked up one of them. I repaired the copy; the patch A receives was never affected. It goes to RETRO 416.
